title: Kindling Splitter in Cast Iron – Split Without an Axe in Your Hand
descriptionHtml:
The axe slips and your hand is always too close

Kindling is the fiddliest thing there is to split. The piece of wood is too small to hold steady, the axe bounces off the knots, and every swing is taken with the hand closer to the blade than it should be. It ends up with you buying bagged kindling instead.

The log stays still – you strike from above

Place the log in the ring and drive it down onto the wedge with a mallet. The ring holds the piece upright through the whole blow, the wedge does the work, and your hand never needs to be near the blade. The splitter stands firmly on a cast base and takes blow after blow.

The lifestyle image is an AI-generated illustration.

Features

  • Hands stay away from the blade – you strike from above with a mallet, the wedge sits still at the bottom
  • The wood doesn't fly off on a half blow – the ring holds the piece upright all the way down
  • Can stand outside and be struck – cast iron throughout the splitter, 0.72 kg
  • Takes a normal piece of kindling – 12.5 cm inner diameter in the ring, 27 cm high
  • Stands firmly without being screwed down – cast base of 14.5 cm, set it on a stump and start

Change of mind

You have 14 days to change your mind, counted from the day you receive the item.
